questions.key_step: Complementary-angle condition cos^2 a + cos^2 b = 1 gives a biquadratic; reject x<0.
questions.justification: Routine chain: convert, solve x^2 quadratic, check sign; no hidden idea.
questions.nearest_anchor: 2023-P2-Q3 (L3) - easier, no range trap beyond sign

questions.key_step: Compare the triangular wave with |sin x| using sin t < t.
questions.justification: Graph reading plus one inequality; only three touching points, little casework.
Single standard move applied twice; proof of a given identity.

questions.key_step: Branch condition: pi is added only when cotA*cot^3A > 1.
questions.justification: Needs the case split of the tan^-1 addition rule and the sign of the combined argument; two cases.

questions.key_step: cos^-1(x/sqrt(1+x^2)) = cot^-1 x, so f = 3pi/4 - 2tan^-1 x.
questions.justification: Recognise one identity, solve a simple inequality with tan(3pi/8).
Single well-known telescoping move, then lowest terms.
Disguised telescoping needs the right factorisation but is a familiar pattern.

questions.key_step: Principal values of cos^-1(sin 2) and sec^-1(cosec 10), then range of 6x^2/(x^4+1).
questions.justification: Three sub-parts, Vieta, careful principal-value reduction of angles 2 and 10, range by discriminant.

questions.key_step: theta=cos^-1 x lies in [2pi/3,pi] so 3theta lies in [2pi,3pi] and cos^-1(cos3theta)=3theta-2pi.
questions.justification: Branch identification for the 3x-4x^3 pattern is not routine but is a known drill.

questions.key_step: Half-angle squares as 2/(1-cos t), rationalise with alpha^2+beta^2=14.
questions.justification: Surd algebra with cancellation of sqrt14; moderate computation, no real insight.

questions.key_step: p and (sin^-1 y)^2 as roots of a quadratic; ranges cut integer K to 2.
questions.justification: Quadratic-roots viewpoint plus principal-range bounding for the upper limit of K; most students stop at D>=0.

questions.key_step: Solve in the inverse function, intersect with range, invert through a monotone function.
questions.justification: Three routine inequalities, each one or two steps.

questions.key_step: Product of two ratios gives tan^2x tan^2y<1; range intersections in (c).
questions.justification: Part (b) needs a small insight, (a) and (c) range care; three parts.

questions.key_step: Powers of a proper fraction decrease; inverse layers cancel.
Sum of three GPs combine into x+x^2+x^3+...
questions.justification: Two routine steps (cancel inverses, sum GP).

questions.key_step: Equal GP factor cancels, giving x = x^2+x^3 and 2sin18 degrees.
questions.justification: Chain: GP sums, cancel, solve quadratic, recognise sin 18 degrees.

questions.key_step: Parity of four functions using tan^-1(-t)=-tan^-1 t and cot^-1(-t)=pi-cot^-1 t.
questions.justification: Four short, routine parity checks; (B) needs one care step.

questions.key_step: For each of four maps decide one-one, into, odd, invertible and periodic.
questions.justification: Four items with five properties each; domain/codomain care (A, B, C, D); no deep idea.

questions.key_step: Reduce each modulus expression on the correct interval; (D) domain is {-1,1}.
questions.justification: Four items, each with case work and domain traps; the (D) domain trap is the non-routine part.
